**Best all-around pick: [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).** Its 2,073.6 Wh capacity is the strongest option in the results for keeping a reptile heater running through a longer outage. The cited estimate is about a day for a 100 W ceramic heat emitter on a thermostat; actual runtime varies with how often the heater runs and power-conversion losses. [Source and estimate](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage)

For a small enclosure using a **24 W heat mat** and a shorter backup window, the [BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage) is a smaller, lower-cost option; the source estimates roughly 6–8 hours. A heat mat generally draws less power than a heat lamp, so it can last longer on the same station.

Whichever you choose, keep the heater controlled by its **thermostat**, and test your setup before an outage. Insulating the enclosure can also help conserve heat; [Petco’s outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage) recommends insulating the habitat and having backup heat plans.
